predecessors.note: The League was formed in 1576 (confraternities) and allied with Philip II at Joinville on 31 December 1584, but held land from May 1588.

land.text: the League-held towns and provinces returned to Henry IV, Paris in March 1594, Mayenne in January 1596, Mercœur at Angers on 20 March 1598

capitals.name: Paris

region.text: Mercœur's Brittany: 'organized a government at Nantes'

ledger.note: 1588: Mercœur takes Brittany into the League. 'In 1588 Mercœur joined the Catholic League in Brittany' and, claiming the duchy through his wife, 'endeavoured to make himself independent monarch of the region'; the French Wars of Religion page: he 'organized a government at Nantes'. A 60 km disc round Nantes is my reading; the pages list no other Breton town.

region.text: Paris, under the Committee of Sixteen

ledger.note: May 1588: the Day of the Barricades; Henry III flees Paris and the League holds it. 'The Committee of Sixteen took complete control of the government' (FWR page, May 1588); League page: 'On the Day of the Barricades, Henry III was forced to flee Paris, leaving Guise as de facto ruler of France'. Infobox seat: Paris and Péronne.

region.text: Aix-en-Provence, which fell to the League's armies in 1589

ledger.note: 1589: Aix-en-Provence falls to the League's armies. Page: a man 'was arrested in 1589 when Aix-en-Provence fell to the League's armies'. The page names no other Provençal town; the 40 km disc is my reading.

region.text: Dijon and Mayenne's governorship of Burgundy

ledger.note: 5 January 1589: Mayenne secures Dijon for the Holy Union. 'only when Mayenne himself arrived on 5 January was Dijon secured for the Sainte Union'; his governorship was Burgundy. A 60 km disc round Dijon is my reading of the Burgundian governorship.

4 March 1589: Mayenne installs a League provincial council at Rouen. 'Mayenne himself visited Rouen on 4 March, to install a ligueur provincial council'; French Wars of Religion page: Mayenne 'controlled most of rural Normandy'. Normandy is drawn whole as my reading; the pages do not list its towns.

region.text: Arques (September 1589) to Ivry (14 March 1590), Mayenne's Normandy

ledger.note: September 1589: Henry IV defeats Mayenne at Arques. After Henry III was killed, Henry of Navarre held 'the south and west', with the League holding 'the north and east'; at Arques Henry 'inflicted a severe defeat on the Duke'. Normandy is the campaign zone on my reading.

1590: Henry IV besieges Paris. 'Henry was victorious at the Battle of Arques and the Battle of Ivry, but failed to take Paris after besieging it in 1590.' The French Wars of Religion page: the siege was lifted by Spanish forces under Parma.
1590: the Spanish under Parma lift the siege of Paris, which 'prepared to fight to the death rather than accept a Calvinist king'.

region.text: Arques (September 1589) to Ivry (14 March 1590), Mayenne's Normandy

ledger.note: 14 March 1590: Henry IV wins at Ivry. 'key victory for Henry against forces led by the Duke of Mayenne'. The Normandy campaign ends without the League losing the province in the pages read.

1594: Normandy returns to Henry IV. The pages opened are silent on when Rouen and Normandy left the League (the French Wars of Religion page says only that the 1591-1592 siege of Rouen repeated Paris); bridged at the fall of Paris.

region.text: Paris, under the Committee of Sixteen

ledger.note: 22 March 1594: Henry IV enters Paris. 'He entered Paris on 22 March 1594 and was welcomed with jubilation' (Mayenne left on 6 March 1594; the League page gives 27 February 1594 for his welcome, which is the Chartres coronation date on the Henry IV page).

region.text: Aix-en-Provence, which fell to the League's armies in 1589

ledger.note: 1596: the League's Aix-en-Provence is no longer League-held. The pages opened are silent on when Provence returned; bridged at Mayenne's January 1596 submission.

region.text: Dijon and Mayenne's governorship of Burgundy

ledger.note: January 1596: Mayenne submits and Burgundy returns to the crown. 'By his submission in January 1596 he was returned to loyalty'; after Fontaine-Française (July 1595) he abandoned the Spanish. The page does not say Burgundy itself changed hands.

region.text: Mercœur's Brittany: 'organized a government at Nantes'

ledger.note: 20 March 1598: Mercœur submits at Angers, the last of the League. Page: Henry 'received his submission at Angers on 20 March 1598, the last member of the League to do so'.

region.text: Mercœur's Brittany, the last League land

ledger.note: March 1598: the League ends with Mercœur's submission; the Edict of Nantes follows on 13 April 1598. 'received his submission at Angers on 20 March 1598'.

wars.name: War of the Three Henrys
wars.outcome: The war 'took place during 1585–1589'; the Barricades (May 1588) put Paris in the League's hands, the Guises were assassinated on 23-24 December 1588 and Henry III was killed at Saint-Cloud in August 1589.
wars.note: Treaty of Joinville with Philip II, 31 December 1584; Treaty of Nemours, 7 July 1585 (FWR page).

wars.name: French Wars of Religion (League phase)
wars.outcome: Henry IV defeated the League at Arques (1589) and Ivry (1590), converted on 25 July 1593 and entered Paris on 22 March 1594; Mayenne submitted in January 1596, Mercœur on 20 March 1598, and the Edict of Nantes followed on 13 April 1598.
wars.note: Spain backed the League (Joinville 1584, Parma 1590, Craon 1592) and fought Henry IV in 1595-1598 (Amiens, March-September 1597; Peace of Vervins, 2 May 1598).

certainty.note: City garrisons and governorships with no boundary record; the discs are my drawing.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from six pages (Catholic League (French), French Wars of Religion, Charles de Lorraine Duke of Mayenne, Philippe Emmanuel Duke of Mercoeur, War of the Three Henrys, Henry IV of France). The League page and the war pages are thin on the lands the League held: they name Paris, Dijon, Rouen/Normandy, Aix-en-Provence and Nantes and give "the north and east" (July 1589) as a generic description. The map therefore draws only those five lands as discs or the whole of Normandy; Reims, Lyon, Toulouse, Orleans, Champagne and Picardy (League-held in the Wars of Religion) are not on the pages and are not drawn. A gap-filler should open "Siege of Rouen (1591-1592)", "Siege of Paris (1590)" and the Sainte Union city lists.
NAME/SLUG: 'Catholic League (France)' = slug catholic-league-france, so as not to collide with the German Catholic League (1609-1635) that another group may write as catholic-league.
DISCREPANCIES: the League page puts Henry IV's welcome in Paris on 27 February 1594; the War of the Three Henrys page gives 22 March 1594 and the Mayenne page says Mayenne left on 6 March 1594; the Henry IV page gives 27 February 1594 for the Chartres coronation (Reims was League-held). Henry III's death is "July 1589" (FWR page), "August 1589" (War of the Three Henrys, Henry IV) and 1 August 1589 (League page).
CONFIDENCE 1: the 1594 Normandy loss and the 1596 Aix loss (page silent on when they returned). The Kingdom of France dossier (kingdom-of-france) does not carry the matching loss events (it covers the Wars of Religion only from Henry IV's 1589 war); the compile should treat this rebel dossier's gain/loss against kingdom-of-france as the carve-out.
Not covered: the Huguenot side (Huguenots: Cliopatria 1622-1631, group eu-10), the Treaty of Nemours terms, Folembray (January 1596), Vervins (2 May 1598, on the FWR page only as a war end).
